title: Multimodal Volumetric Retinal Imaging by Oblique Scanning Laser Ophthalmoscopy (oSLO) and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT)
protocol: Use a supercontinuum laser source as the system laser source.
Separate the visible light range (450-650 nm) from higher wavelength range (650-2000 nm) by a dichroic mirror (DM1).
Expand the spectrum with a pair of dispersive prisms after the beam passing through a polarization beam splitter (PBS).
Place a slit to select the excitation wavelength range (475-495 nm).
Use a reflective mirror to reflect the filtered beam back to the prism pair and then couple the light into a single mode fiber (SMF 1).
Use a spectrometer to confirm the wavelength selection at the output of the single mode fiber.
Connect the single mode fiber to two cascaded optical fiber couplers as shown in Figure 2.
Deflect the laser by a galvanometer mirror (GM1).
Relay the laser to a second galvanometer mirror (GM2) by a 1:1 telescope system, and further relay to the pupil of the eye by a 3:1 telescope system.
Install a dichroic mirror (DM2) within the 3:1 telescope system to reflect the fluorescence signals.
Mount the 3:1 telescope system and the dichroic mirror (DM2) on a customized dove tail slider.
Use a caliper to precisely control the offset length as desired.
Reflect the fluorescence by the dichroic mirror and relay it to the third galvanometer mirror to de-scan the slow scanning.
Relay the light to an imaging objective lens using another 1:1 telescope system.
Install the above optics on a translation stage.
Mount a final imaging system on a stage with three degrees of freedom (rotation, and two axis of translation).
Use a planar camera to capture the cross-sectional fluorescence images.
Separate the near infrared (NIR) range (650-900 nm) from the remaining light (650-2000 nm) by another dichroic mirror (DM3).
Use a long pass filter to further limit the bandwidth to 800-900 nm.
Couple the beam into a single mode fiber (SMF 2).
Connect the single mode fiber to one input port of the first optical fiber coupler.
Direct light from the second output port of the second fiber coupler to the OCT reference arm.
Insert a variable neutral density filter (VNDF) in the OCT reference arm.
Add dispersion compensation plates in the OCT reference arm.
Place a reflective mirror at the end of the OCT reference arm.
Use data acquisition system software written in LabVIEW.
Output an 80% duty cycle saw tooth with 500 steps using AO1 to control GM2 for each B-scan.
Trigger the line scan camera at each step during forward scanning direction.
Set exposure time for the line scan camera to 17 µs.
Repeat measurement 5 times at the same B-scan location to acquire OCTA signal.
Set AO output rate at 100 kHz.
Set OCT A-line rate at 50 kHz.
Control y' slow scanning mirror, GM1, with a ramping waveform.
Synchronize de-scanning mirror, GM3, with GM1 for synchronization.
Trigger the planar camera using AO2 to capture one fluorescent image at each y' location.
Adjust the slit in the oSLO light source to select blue excitation wavelength.
Monitor the spectral range with a spectrometer, ensuring it is around 475-490 nm.
Shift the optical axis by ~5 mm using the dove tail mount slider.
Translate the fluorescence detection optics stage by the same 5 mm.
Adjust the final fluorescence imaging system to be ~30°.
Measure the optical power using a power meter.
Ensure blue oSLO excitation power is ≤0.2 mW and OCT laser power ≤0.8 mW.
Transfer a 12-weeks male Long Evans rat into the induction chamber.
Anesthetize the rat with 4.5% isoflurane in oxygen for 10 minutes at a flow rate of 2 L/min.
Confirm depth of anesthesia by checking lack of withdrawal reflex during interdigital pinch.
Place the rat on a 5-axis holder after induction.
Provide supplemental heat using a heated stage or circulating warm water blanket.
Maintain anesthesia at 1.5% isofluorane with a flow rate of 2 liters/minute.
Dilate the pupil with 1% Tropicamide ophthalmic solution for 2 minutes.
Apply 0.5% Tetracaine HCl ophthalmic solution on the rat's eye if necessary.
Keep the eye moisturized with commercial artificial tears at least once every minute.
Inject fluorescein salt or FITC diluted in sterile saline through the tail vein using a 1 mL syringe and a 29G needle.
Turn on the laser source.
Place a neutral density filter to attenuate the blue light excitation during alignment.
Measure the power of the OCT light to be ~0.8 mW, and the blue light <0.01 mW.
Start the galvanometer scanning and alignment mode.
Adjust the height of the eye ball to make a stationary laser spot on the cornea.
Adjust the rat eye position to make the rim of the pupil roughly perpendicular to the laser.
Offset the laser to the apical center of the eye to about ~1.5 mm.
Adjust the animal holder until OCT images reach optimal quality.
Ensure that the cross-sectional B-scan image in the x' fast scanning direction appears flat.
Switch to the y' slow scanning direction and ensure the cross-section B-scan image appears tilted due to oblique scanning.
Remove the neutral density filter to the blue light excitation.
Monitor the real time feed from the camera for a cross-sectional fluorescent image showing blood vessels at different depths.
Adjust the focus of the final fluorescence imaging system to reach optimal focus.
Allow fine adjustments of the eye position in the lateral plane to reach optimal oSLO image quality.
After alignment, start acquiring simultaneous OCTA and volumetric fluorescein angiography (vFA).
Construct volumetric images for both OCTA and oSLO using previously described algorithms.
Generate depth-resolved retinal vasculatures by image segmentation.
Turn off the laser after imaging is completed.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes of the animal.
Place the animal in a recovery box and do not leave it unattended until it regains sufficient consciousness.
